 All eyes on Future Subtropical Storm Kyle as coastal storm brews off Southeast this weekend
 A coastal storm could threaten travel plans for millions of people along or heading to the Southeast coast for Thanksgiving.
 By
 Alexandra Myers , Julian Atienza 
 Source
 FOX Weather
 Facebook 
 Twitter 
 Email 
 Copy Link
 02:12 Chances of development for Subtropical Storm Kyle increase for the next seven days 
 POTENTIAL SUBTROPICAL STORM LOOMS IN ATLANTIC: Seemingly never-ending storms continue to slam Florida, bringing another multiday flood threat as potential Subtropical Storm Kyle lingers in the Atlantic with increasing odds.
 THE TAKEAWAY 
 A potential coastal storm could form off Georgia, South Carolina and Florida's coast by this weekend.
 The National Hurricane Center is monitoring the area where the system is expected to emerge for potential tropical development.
 A Level 2 out of 4 flash flood risk is in place due to heavy rain, gusty winds and high surf.
 Forecasters are monitoring two possible scenarios, with the storm's track and strength playing a major role in how significant the impacts could be.
 The same system responsible for bringing a weeklong flash flood threat to Florida could develop into future Subtropical Storm Kyle by the weekend and threaten early Thanksgiving travel plans for millions of people as the National Hurricane Center (NHC) designated the area off the Southeast coast as an area to watch for tropical development.
 FLORIDA GOVERNOR DECLARES STATE OF EMERGENCY AS DEADLY FLOODING GRIPS SUNSHINE STATE 
 Area to watch for tropical development
 (FOX Weather) 
  According to the NHC, future Kyle has the potential to take on some subtropical characteristics, but is currently being given low odds of development over the next seven days.
 While there's growing consensus among computer forecast models that a storm will form off the coast this weekend, there is still uncertainty surrounding exactly where it will track and how strong the storm will become.
 The overview of the expected impacts from the storm.
 (FOX Weather) 
  WEST COAST BRACES FOR RELENTLESS BARRAGE OF STORMS AS POWERFUL ATMOSPHERIC RIVER FUELS HEAVY RAIN, STRONG SURF 
 Forecasters are monitoring two possible scenarios, with the storm's eventual track and strength playing a major role in determining how significant the impacts could be.
 The first scenario involves a more westerly track.
 Flooding and heavy rain in Savannah, Georgia on Saturday, Aug. 2, 2025. 
 (Brandy Campbell/FOX Weather / FOX Weather) 
 If the storm develops into a stronger system along this track, it could bring more widespread, heavy rain along the coast, with rainfall extending inland across the Carolinas and Georgia into Saturday evening and Sunday as the storm moves north.
 A track closer to the coastline would also allow for stronger, gusty winds , increasing the potential for coastal erosion and high surf.
 WHAT IS COASTAL EROSION AND WHY IS IT DANGEROUS? 
 The amount of rain expected.
 (FOX Weather) 
  But, if the storm remains weaker while following a westerly track, rain and gusty winds would be possible mainly along the coast, with only spotty showers inland. Waves and surf could still be elevated, but overall impacts would likely be minor.
 SUPER EL NIÑO DECLARED AS FORECASTERS WARN OF MAJOR SHIFTS IN WEATHER DURING WINTER SEASON 
 The second scenario involves a more easterly track, keeping the storm farther offshore.
 If the system develops into a stronger storm along this track, it could bring a quicker burst of gusty winds and rain to coastal areas of the Carolinas and Georgia .
 Flash flood outlook.
 (FOX Weather) 
  However, impacts would likely be shorter-lived as the main steering flow pushes the storm farther out to sea, keeping many of the more significant impacts offshore, the FOX Forecast Center said.
 If the storm remains weaker along the easterly track, impacts would be minimal along the coast, with mostly sunny conditions expected inland.
 A pedestrian navigates a driving rain in Charleston, South Carolina.
 (Scott Olson / Getty Images) 
 Spotty showers and breezy conditions could still develop along the coast through the middle of the weekend.
 The FOX Forecast Center notes that some AI models suggest the coastal storm could develop into a hybrid subtropical low if the system slows down and remains over the warmer waters of the Gulf Stream.
 WHAT IS AN ARKSTORM? THE CATASTROPHIC WEATHER SCENARIO THAT COULD DEVASTATE CALIFORNIA 
 However, forecasters emphasize that the likelihood of this scenario developing remains very low.
 A car drives through flooding in Savannah, Georgia on Saturday, Aug. 2, 2025. 
 (Brandy Campbell/FOX Weather / FOX Weather) 
 Regardless of how the storm develops, the Weather Prediction Center has issued a Level 2 out of 4 flash flood risk across South Carolina , Georgia and northeastern Florida from Saturday into early Sunday morning.
 THANKSGIVING OUTLOOK: EL NIÑO-DRIVEN STORMS THREATEN TO WREAK HAVOC ON HOLIDAY TRAVEL FOR MILLIONS 
 There is also the potential for impacts farther north along the East Coast, although it is still too early to determine how far the storm's effects could extend.
 Stay with FOX Weather as the potential coastal storm develops, and the forecast becomes clearer.
